definition: Bureaucratic means tangled in excessive administrative rules, procedures, and red tape.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word bureaucratic. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know bureaucratic should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Renewing a simple permit became a bureaucratic slog of forms, stamps, and waiting rooms.
A formal process follows set rules, while a bureaucratic one buries you in forms, offices, and approvals.
A bureaucratic system is tangled in red tape, while a labyrinthine one is so maze-like you may never find your way through at all.

Procedural means bound to official steps and formalities, and it is a neutral word: a procedural step may be perfectly sensible. Bureaucratic is the complaint version: the offices, forms, and approvals have multiplied far past what the task needs. A process can be procedural without bothering anyone; it turns bureaucratic when the red tape takes over.

Rule-bound means controlled by rigid regulations, with little freedom to bend or make exceptions. Bureaucratic adds the machinery and the frustration: layers of offices, forms, and approvals that swallow simple tasks. A rule-bound umpire just enforces the rulebook strictly; a bureaucratic agency makes you stand in three lines to file one page.

Ordway wanted one globe for her classroom.
The globe cost nineteen dollars.
The district's ordering system wanted more: a requisition form, a vendor-approval form, a signature from her principal, and a second signature from an assistant superintendent she had never met.
Six weeks in, the request came back -- not denied, just returned, because box 14 had been left blank.
Colleagues told her this was normal.
The purchasing office was so bureaucratic, one veteran said, that buying chalk had once required a committee.
Ordway finally paid the nineteen dollars herself.
The globe arrived in two days, and the requisition form, resubmitted with box 14 filled in, was still winding through approvals in June.
